e-12522.problem:
Find $\boldsymbol f''(\pi,0)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/08502aa81729d4f88aec094e2e2f5c7b4a57825ef3767f1eec29700ceb6e21a3.png)
e-12522.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/025dd1a0b89b52e32a3e42e5bd3492261ed060f104f627051b6950c7f94d66c1.png)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/f1a47569220f01e1dc474a13a5040e969449ee0b10cfe7df39c3aec4c6175f41.png)

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/f0b46d26ccc6fefc404b021bde11c4d6959c00ae0ef1145a9984da602bcc54ef.png)

First, notice that since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/964f8ac9ca9c305faef8562f66d063f318ecbe402df337377bd9efdf61301567.png) 
 we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^y\cos x ,  
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} =e^y\sin x .
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\pi,0).$ This gives

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/540c920abd2989b29aae275eedd179c5118e82354915e591c0d1c5296ca9fa21.png)

e-12524.problem: Find $\boldsymbol f''(1,0)$ for the function $f(x,y)  = x^2 e^y.$
e-12524.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/7444a8128c085d7bf4f56a57a60c260864a50da0b744b6dbe22a2ced89a0588d.png)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/22dd960829ea268e5aade685b56949f8998f87ae8c040a90f04436cbfc6b9a58.png)

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/4fede2bb5c2306f62b55b7996488baee52c69e7d41b011e0e9d2b7405e63a8f4.png)

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})={x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{ }\,{e}^{y} & 2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ 2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $\left(1,0\right).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,0)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-12523.problem:
Given that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/b3e96b1a54af842b69da4ae5fcb44858bffdac48b27cde6677c15c05906e890d.png) 
 evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(0,1).$
e-12523.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/af5524049f5f8b3c4c4241520f2d874b454d61b1b025362f5193437f766e610b.png)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/8882516e2732e419efdfb8439265212dd4f380d6a6ea58f6ff1291030bf50bfb.png)

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det \left( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \right)
$$

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/4fede2bb5c2306f62b55b7996488baee52c69e7d41b011e0e9d2b7405e63a8f4.png)

First, notice that since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/9252d1ce4f5df828f45351d01e0709cf2f2ca5df2c9c25390c111f40ca00fb22.png) we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = \ln y, 
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} = \dfrac xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{1}{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,1) = 0 \cdot 0 - 1\cdot 1 = -1.
$$

decision.explanation: Differentiating the given first partial derivatives gives f_xx=-2y, f_xy=f_yx=1-2x, and f_yy=0. At (1,2), the Hessian is [[-4,-1],[-1,0]], which is option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(1,2)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y-2xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x-{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2xy)=-2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-{x}^{2})=1-2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2xy)=1-2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{x}^{2})=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$

Question 1
?

Find f″(1,2) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[y−2xyx−x2]

a
[3−1−12]
b
[−422−1]
c
[−4−1−10]
d
[2220]
e
[2−1−1−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[y−2xyx−x2], we must have

∂f∂x=y−2xy,∂f∂y=x−x2.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(y−2xy)=−2y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x−x2)=1−2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(y−2xy)=1−2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x−x2)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[−2y1−2x1−2x0].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (1,2). This gives

f″(1,2)=[−4−1−10].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(1,2)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y-2xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x-{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2xy)=-2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-{x}^{2})=1-2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2xy)=1-2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{x}^{2})=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2y & 1-2x \\ 1-2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(1,2).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(1,2)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=10xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=5{x}^{2}-2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy)=10y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=10x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy)=10x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

Find f″(12,12) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[10xy5x2−2y]

a
[52020−2]
b
[1055−2]
c
[20−5−5−2]
d
[51010−2]
e
[555−2]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[10xy5x2−2y], we must have

∂f∂x=10xy,∂f∂y=5x2−2y.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(10xy)=10y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(5x2−2y)=10x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(10xy)=10x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(5x2−2y)=−2

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[10y10x10x−2].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (12,12). This gives

f″(12,12)=[555−2].

verification.explanation: Rechecking gives f_xx=10y, f_xy=f_yx=10x, and f_yy=-2. At (1/2,1/2), this yields [[5,5],[5,-2]], confirming option e and agreeing with the revealed solution. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=10xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=5{x}^{2}-2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy)=10y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=10x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy)=10x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[e−e2−x2y]

a
[e2−x002]
b
[−e2−x000]
c
[e−x002]
d
[e002]
e
[−e2002]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since e is constant, differentiating e-e^(2-x) with respect to x gives e^(2-x) by the chain rule. Both mixed partial derivatives are zero, and differentiating 2y with respect to y gives 2. Thus the Hessian is option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=e-{e}^{2-x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(e-{e}^{2-x})={e}^{2-x}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)=0 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(e-{e}^{2-x})=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)=2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2-x} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[e−e2−x2y]

a
[e2−x002]
b
[−e2−x000]
c
[e−x002]
d
[e002]
e
[−e2002]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[e−e2−x2y], we must have

∂f∂x=e−e2−x,∂f∂y=2y.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(e−e2−x)=e2−x∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(2y)=0∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(e−e2−x)=0∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(2y)=2

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[e2−x002].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=e-{e}^{2-x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(e-{e}^{2-x})={e}^{2-x}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)=0 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(e-{e}^{2-x})=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)=2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2-x} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[−4y+13y2−4x−1]

a
[2x660]
b
[−2y4x4x0]
c
[0−4−46y]
d
[6y4x4x0]
e
[04x4x−4y]
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating f_x=-4y+1 and f_y=3y^2-4x-1 gives f_xx=0, f_xy=f_yx=-4, and f_yy=6y. The resulting Hessian matches option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-4y+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}-4x-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4y+1)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y+1)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=6y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -4 & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y) given that f′(x,y)=[−4y+13y2−4x−1]

a
[2x660]
b
[−2y4x4x0]
c
[0−4−46y]
d
[6y4x4x0]
e
[04x4x−4y]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[−4y+13y2−4x−1], we must have

∂f∂x=−4y+1,∂f∂y=3y2−4x−1.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(−4y+1)=0∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(3y2−4x−1)=−4∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(−4y+1)=−4∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(3y2−4x−1)=6y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[0−4−46y].

verification.explanation: Rechecking gives f_xx=0, f_xy=f_yx=-4, and f_yy=6y, confirming option c and matching the revealed solution. The incorrect feedback applies to the deliberately submitted option b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-4y+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}-4x-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4y+1)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y+1)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=6y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -4 & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y & 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(2,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

a
[0−2−20]
b
[2004]
c
[222−22]
d
[222−4]
e
[200−4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[2xsin⁡yx2cos⁡y], we must have

∂f∂x=2xsin⁡y,∂f∂y=x2cos⁡y.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2xsin⁡y)=2sin⁡y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x2cos⁡y)=2xcos⁡y∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2xsin⁡y)=2xcos⁡y∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x2cos⁡y)=−x2sin⁡y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[2sin⁡y2xcos⁡y2xcos⁡y−x2sin⁡y].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (2,π2). This gives

f″(2,π2)=[200−4].

content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y & 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(2,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[2xsin⁡yx2cos⁡y], we must have

∂f∂x=2xsin⁡y,∂f∂y=x2cos⁡y.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2xsin⁡y)=2sin⁡y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x2cos⁡y)=2xcos⁡y∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2xsin⁡y)=2xcos⁡y∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x2cos⁡y)=−x2sin⁡y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[2sin⁡y2xcos⁡y2xcos⁡y−x2sin⁡y].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (2,π2). This gives

f″(2,π2)=[200−4].

decision.explanation: For f(x,y)=(y-1)(x^2-1), the second partial derivatives are f_xx=2(y-1), f_xy=f_yx=2x, and f_yy=0. At (-1,2), the Hessian is [[2,-2],[-2,0]], matching option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x(y-1) & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(y-1))=2(y-1)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-1)=2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(y-1))=2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2(y-1) & 2x \\ 2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-1,2).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-1,2)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find f″(−1,2) for the function f(x,y)=(y−1)(x2−1).

a
[2002]
b
[2−2−20]
c
[0220]
d
[122−1]
e
[0−1−12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x((y−1)(x2−1))∂∂y((y−1)(x2−1))]=[2x(y−1)x2−1]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2x(y−1))=2(y−1)∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x2−1)=2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2x(y−1))=2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x2−1)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[2(y−1)2x2x0].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (−1,2). This gives

f″(−1,2)=[2−2−20].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x(y-1) & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(y-1))=2(y-1)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-1)=2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(y-1))=2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2(y-1) & 2x \\ 2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-1,2).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-1,2)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=xsin⁡y+xy.

a
[−1cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1xcos⁡y]
b
[0cos⁡y+xcos⁡y+xsin⁡y]
c
[ycos⁡x11−xsin⁡y]
d
[ycos⁡x00−xsin⁡y]
e
[0cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1−xsin⁡y]
Submit

decision.explanation: The first partial derivatives are f_x=sin(y)+y and f_y=x cos(y)+x. Differentiating again gives f_xx=0, f_xy=f_yx=cos(y)+1, and f_yy=-x sin(y), matching option e.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y & x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 & -x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=xsin⁡y+xy.

a
[−1cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1xcos⁡y]
b
[0cos⁡y+xcos⁡y+xsin⁡y]
c
[ycos⁡x11−xsin⁡y]
d
[ycos⁡x00−xsin⁡y]
e
[0cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1−xsin⁡y]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(xsin⁡y+xy)∂∂y(xsin⁡y+xy)]=[sin⁡y+yxcos⁡y+x]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(sin⁡y+y)=0∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(xcos⁡y+x)=cos⁡y+1∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(sin⁡y+y)=cos⁡y+1∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(xcos⁡y+x)=−xsin⁡y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[0cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1−xsin⁡y].

verification.explanation: Rechecking gives f_xx=0, f_xy=f_yx=cos(y)+1, and f_yy=-x sin(y). This confirms option e and agrees with the revealed solution. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y & x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 & -x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function

history.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y & x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 & -x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(xsin⁡y+xy)∂∂y(xsin⁡y+xy)]=[sin⁡y+yxcos⁡y+x]

f″(x,y)=[0cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1−xsin⁡y].

before.html:
Question 8
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=ex2+y2.

a
[(2+4x2)ex2+y24xyex2+y24xyex2+y2(2+4y2)ex2+y2]
b
[(2+4x)ex2+y22ex2+y22ex2+y2(2+4y)ex2+y2]
c
[(2+4x2)ex2+y200(2+4y2)ex2+y2]
d
[ex2+y22ex2+y22ex2+y2ex2+y2]
e
[(2+4x2)ex2+y22ex2+y22ex2+y2(2+4y2)ex2+y2]
Submit

decision.explanation: The first partial derivatives are f_x=2x e^(x^2+y^2) and f_y=2y e^(x^2+y^2). Applying the product and chain rules gives f_xx=(2+4x^2)e^(x^2+y^2), f_xy=f_yx=4xy e^(x^2+y^2), and f_yy=(2+4y^2)e^(x^2+y^2), matching option a.

Question 8
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=ex2+y2.

a
[(2+4x2)ex2+y24xyex2+y24xyex2+y2(2+4y2)ex2+y2]
b
[(2+4x)ex2+y22ex2+y22ex2+y2(2+4y)ex2+y2]
c
[(2+4x2)ex2+y200(2+4y2)ex2+y2]
d
[ex2+y22ex2+y22ex2+y2ex2+y2]
e
[(2+4x2)ex2+y22ex2+y22ex2+y2(2+4y2)ex2+y2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(ex2+y2)∂∂y(ex2+y2)]=[2xex2+y22yex2+y2]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2xex2+y2)=(2+4x2)ex2+y2∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(2yex2+y2)=4xyex2+y2∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2xex2+y2)=4xyex2+y2∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(2yex2+y2)=(2+4y2)ex2+y2

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[(2+4x2)ex2+y24xyex2+y24xyex2+y2(2+4y2)ex2+y2].

Question 9
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=exy.

a
[exyexy(1+xy)exy(1+xy)exy]
b
[y2exyexy(1+xy)exy(1+xy)x2exy]
c
[y2exyexyexyx2exy]
d
[exyexy+xyexy+xyexy]
e
[x2exyexy(2+xy)exy(2+xy)y2exy]
Submit

decision.explanation: The first partial derivatives are f_x=y e^(xy) and f_y=x e^(xy). Differentiating again gives f_xx=y^2 e^(xy), f_xy=f_yx=(1+xy)e^(xy), and f_yy=x^2 e^(xy), matching option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}y{e}^{xy} & x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{xy})={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{xy})={e}^{xy}+xy\,\text{ }{e}^{xy} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy})={e}^{xy}+xy\,\text{ }{e}^{xy}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{xy})={x}^{2}{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}{e}^{xy} & {e}^{xy}(1+xy) \\ {e}^{xy}(1+xy) & {x}^{2}{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=exy.

a
[exyexy(1+xy)exy(1+xy)exy]
b
[y2exyexy(1+xy)exy(1+xy)x2exy]
c
[y2exyexyexyx2exy]
d
[exyexy+xyexy+xyexy]
e
[x2exyexy(2+xy)exy(2+xy)y2exy]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(exy)∂∂y(exy)]=[yexyxexy]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(yexy)=y2exy∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(xexy)=exy+xy exy∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(yexy)=exy+xy exy∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(xexy)=x2exy

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[y2exyexy(1+xy)exy(1+xy)x2exy].

verification.explanation: Rechecking gives f_xx=y^2 e^(xy), f_xy=f_yx=(1+xy)e^(xy), and f_yy=x^2 e^(xy), confirming option b and matching the revealed solution. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option d.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}y{e}^{xy} & x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{xy})={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{xy})={e}^{xy}+xy\,\text{ }{e}^{xy} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy})={e}^{xy}+xy\,\text{ }{e}^{xy}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{xy})={x}^{2}{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}{e}^{xy} & {e}^{xy}(1+xy) \\ {e}^{xy}(1+xy) & {x}^{2}{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=y2(x2−1).

a
[22y2y2(x2−1)]
b
[2y2x2x2(x2−1)]
c
[2y24xy4xy2(x2−1)]
d
[2y002(x2−1)]
e
[2y2xy2xy2(x2−1)]
Submit

decision.explanation: The first partial derivatives are f_x=2xy^2 and f_y=2y(x^2-1). Differentiating again gives f_xx=2y^2, f_xy=f_yx=4xy, and f_yy=2(x^2-1), matching option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2} & 2y({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y({x}^{2}-1))=4xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2})=4xy\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y({x}^{2}-1))=2({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & 4xy \\ 4xy & 2({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Find f″(x,y) for the function f(x,y)=y2(x2−1).

a
[22y2y2(x2−1)]
b
[2y2x2x2(x2−1)]
c
[2y24xy4xy2(x2−1)]
d
[2y002(x2−1)]
e
[2y2xy2xy2(x2−1)]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(y2(x2−1))∂∂y(y2(x2−1))]=[2xy22y(x2−1)]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2xy2)=2y2∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(2y(x2−1))=4xy∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2xy2)=4xy∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(2y(x2−1))=2(x2−1)

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[2y24xy4xy2(x2−1)].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2} & 2y({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2})=2{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y({x}^{2}-1))=4xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2})=4xy\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y({x}^{2}-1))=2({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2} & 4xy \\ 4xy & 2({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}4xy-3{y}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=4xy-3{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2{x}^{2}-6xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy-3{y}^{2})=4y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}-6xy)=4x-6y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4xy-3{y}^{2})=4x-6y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}-6xy)=-6x\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Question 12
?

Given that f′(x,y)=[ycos⁡(xy)xcos⁡(xy)], evaluate the Hessian determinant of f(x,y) at the point (π,−1).

a
−1
b
1
c
−π2
d
1−2π2
e
π2
Submit

decision.explanation: The second partial derivatives are f_xx=-y^2 sin(xy), f_xy=f_yx=cos(xy)-xy sin(xy), and f_yy=-x^2 sin(xy). At (π,-1), sin(-π)=0 and cos(-π)=-1, so the Hessian is [[0,-1],[-1,0]]. Its determinant is 0-1=-1, matching option a.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Given that 
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}],$ 
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(\pi ,-1).$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=-{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(\pi ,-1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(\pi ,-1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(\pi ,-1)=0\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot (-1)=-1.
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

H(x)=det(f″(x))

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[ycos⁡(xy)xcos⁡(xy)], we must have ∂f∂x=ycos⁡(xy),∂f∂y=xcos⁡(xy).

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(ycos⁡(xy))=−y2sin⁡(xy)∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(xcos⁡(xy))=cos⁡(xy)−xysin⁡(xy)∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(ycos⁡(xy))=cos⁡(xy)−xysin⁡(xy)∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(xcos⁡(xy))=−x2sin⁡(xy)

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2]=[−y2sin⁡(xy)cos⁡(xy)−xysin⁡(xy)cos⁡(xy)−xysin⁡(xy)−x2sin⁡(xy)].

Evaluating the second derivative at (π,−1), we obtain f″(π,−1)=[0−1−10].

Finally, we have H(π,−1)=0⋅0−(−1)⋅(−1)=−1.

For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$

$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=-{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(\pi ,-1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(\pi ,-1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(\pi ,-1)=0\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot (-1)=-1.
$$

before.problem:
Given that

after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+6x-4y & 4{y}^{3}-4x+8y\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=3{x}^{2}+6x-4y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=4{y}^{3}-4x+8y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+6x-4y)=6x+6\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{y}^{3}-4x+8y)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+6x-4y)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{y}^{3}-4x+8y)=12{y}^{2}+8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6x+6 & -4 \\ -4 & 12{y}^{2}+8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,0),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,0)=[\begin{aligned}12 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,0)=12\cdot 8-(-4)\cdot (-4)=80.
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn), the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

The Hessian determinant H(x,y) is the determinant of the second derivative: H(x)=det(f″(x))

In our case, we have f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[3x2+6x−4y4y3−4x+8y], we must have ∂f∂x=3x2+6x−4y,∂f∂y=4y3−4x+8y.

So, the second derivative is f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2]=[6x+6−4−412y2+8].

Evaluating the second derivative at (1,0), we obtain f″(1,0)=[12−4−48].

Finally, we have H(1,0)=12⋅8−(−4)⋅(−4)=80.

${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}],$ 
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(\pi ,\pi ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x),\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y).
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x))=-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y))=\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x))=\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y))=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(\pi ,\pi ),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(\pi ,\pi )=[\begin{aligned}-\pi  & \pi  \\ \pi  & -\pi \end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(\pi ,\pi )=(-\pi )\cdot (-\pi )-\pi \cdot \pi =0.
$$

Given that f′(x,y)=[ysin⁡(y−x)cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y)], evaluate the Hessian determinant of f(x,y) at the point (π,π).

a
−2π
b
−π
c
π
d
2π
e
0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn), the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

The Hessian determinant H(x,y) is the determinant of the second derivative: H(x)=det(f″(x))

In our case, we have f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[ysin⁡(y−x)cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y)], we must have ∂f∂x=ysin⁡(y−x),∂f∂y=cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y).

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives: ∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(ysin⁡(y−x))=−ycos⁡(x−y)∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y))=sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(ysin⁡(y−x))=sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y))=2sin⁡(x−y)−ycos⁡(x−y)

So, the second derivative is f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2]=[−ycos⁡(x−y)sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)2sin⁡(x−y)−ycos⁡(x−y)].

Evaluating the second derivative at (π,π), we obtain f″(π,π)=[−πππ−π].

Finally, we have H(π,π)=(−π)⋅(−π)−π⋅π=0.

verification.explanation: Rechecking at (π,π) gives f_xx=-π, f_xy=f_yx=π, and f_yy=-π. The Hessian determinant is (-π)(-π)-π·π=0, confirming option e and agreeing with the revealed solution. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option c.

$$

$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2(x-1){y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2(x-1)^{2}y.
$$

$$
